evidence: Broad, glossy ovate leaves accompany white bilaterally symmetric flowers.
Stamens project beyond the corolla and end in brownish anthers.
Green calyces show a broad rounded upper lip, narrower pointed lower portions, and fine hairs.
missingEvidence: A complete flowering shoot showing leaf attachment, leaf proportions, and the spacing of flower groups.

candidateSelection.reason: Sweet basil best combines the broad glossy foliage with the white flowers, projecting stamens, and broad-lipped ribbed calyces. The foliage is less suggestive of the narrower, hairier-leaved alternative.

evidence: Broad, elongated leaf blades arch outward from stout upright stalks.
Leaves have prominent pale midribs, parallel venation and sheathing bases.
Alternate leaf attachment and robust, visibly jointed stalks form a characteristic maize-like vegetative combination.
missingEvidence: A clearly resolved maize ear with silk or terminal tassel would provide stronger separation from other large crop grasses.

candidateSelection.reason: Maize best fits the combined broad arching leaf blades, substantial jointed stalks and alternate sheathing leaf bases; sorghum is a weaker vegetative lookalike.

evidence: Angular, broadly triangular leaf blades have pointed shallow lobes and finely toothed margins.
Hairy stems, curling tendrils, and yellow five-lobed flowers form a combination consistent with cucumber.
Flowers are relatively small compared with the broad leaf blades.
missingEvidence: Attached fruit showing shape and surface texture would provide stronger separation from other Cucumis species.

candidateSelection.reason: Cucumber leads because the pointed, angular, finely toothed leaves occur together with hairy vine stems, curling tendrils, and relatively small yellow five-lobed flowers. Melon shares several traits but is less well supported by the visible leaf shape.

evidence: The white spathe is broad and conspicuously cupped around an elongated cream spadix.
Broad elliptic leaves have pronounced corrugation, entire intact margins, and pointed tips.
Leaf stalks and the upright inflorescence emerge from a basal clump.
counterEvidence: These characters overlap with other broad-leaved Spathiphyllum species and cultivated hybrids.
missingEvidence: A clear lateral view of the spadix base and its attachment relative to the spathe.

evidence: Strongly ribbed, entire, elliptic leaves and a pale spathe surrounding a cylindrical spadix are compatible with this species.
counterEvidence: The especially broad, cupped spathe favors the leading candidate, although its shape is partly affected by folding.
missingEvidence: Spadix-to-spathe attachment detail and an unobstructed view of a complete leaf and petiole.

candidateSelection.reason: The broad, cupped white spathe together with the broad, deeply corrugated leaf blades favors Spathiphyllum cochlearispathum. Peace-lily identity is better supported than the exact species.
